tagline: Two old trails from Gray down to the Ocmulgee.
intro: From downtown Gray, State Route 11 runs north about nine miles through Bradley, Wayside and Round Oak on the line of an old Indian trail. At Round Oak the byway turns west onto Round Oak-Juliette Road, a trail once too, and goes about 12 miles through the pine forest of the Piedmont National Wildlife Refuge to the Ocmulgee River at Juliette.
The road has seen armies. In 1864 opposing forces met along it at the Battle of Sunshine Church, and later that year Sherman's march to the sea came through Jones County the same way.

moments.title: Round Oak
moments.text: Founded as Sylvania in 1807, the settlement later took its name from an ancient oak known as a gathering place for Native Americans.

moments.title: Piedmont National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: By the 1930s cotton had worn these hills down to bare red clay, and the refuge began in 1939 on that abandoned farmland, which is forest again.

moments.title: Juliette
moments.text: Across the Ocmulgee from the old mill village of East Juliette, the main street sets from Fried Green Tomatoes became a tourist district with a working Whistle Stop Cafe.
